children: Oil prices are catapulting higher thanks to renewed escalation across the Middle East, pushing Brent crude futures to roughly $105 a barrel and pressuring stock and bond markets worldwide.

The global benchmark is on track to rise for a fifth session in a row to notch its highest closing level since May. At the same time, the average U.S. price for a gallon of gasoline neared $4.28 Thursday, according to AAA, while diesel approached $6 a gallon.

"As long as oil keeps rising, inflation risks will increase and expectations for Federal Reserve tightening will grow, leaving rates vulnerable to moving higher," Oxford Economics analyst John Canavan wrote in a note to clients.

Along with U.S.-Iran tensions and Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure, attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi militia against Saudi Arabian facilities are adding to supply concerns. On Thursday, OPEC's latest monthly report suggested Saudi crude production in August fell to its lowest level since 1990, according to oil analyst Rory Johnston.
"Wheels coming off," Johnston wrote of the market in a post on X.
